steps.what: Send objectives set by the boards
Draft administrative procedures from the objectives

loop.input: objective rows and the procedure template
loop.output: draft in which each line cites an objective id
loop.check: Every line cites an objective id that is on the form
loop.stop: One pass, then leave a blank where an objective id is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: Local practice is prose and a fixed mail-merge cannot write it

steps.what: Sign the procedures version for this period
File the signed procedures and review date
Oversee procedures that miss an objective

tasks.design: Board members submit objective id, owner, review date and the result they want on a form in {DOCS}. A bounded draft writes administrative procedures in {DOCS} and every line must cite an objective id. The manager signs one version. Only that version is filed, with its review date on the {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures were recopied from old documents, and the board objectives lived in mail, so a draft would have repeated stale aims.
tasks.enabler_now: An objective id can be shared between the board form and the procedure template, so each line can be checked against a field.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing which objective wins when two of them conflict is still a board call.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides which local practice is a real procedure and which exception stays outside the text.

ambition.what: Re-sign procedures when board objectives change, not only at the yearly review

tasks.altitude: Less time retyping sections, more time on exceptions. The manager can refuse a procedure whose lines do not match an objective.

reach.task: Set the objectives the procedures must meet
reach.learn: Which procedure version is signed and which objectives are still uncovered

evidence.claim: In a mid-size community organisation this task is a document plus a meeting. The hard part is which practice becomes a procedure, not the formatting.
Digest [S1] describes policy-library management that versions procedure and policy texts, maps them to rules, and can classify or summarise them. A person still approves.
Digest [S2] describes a European governance, risk and compliance register for policy and control tasks. It is not a measured result for this team.
Digest [S15] describes a published report that contained fabricated citations, after which the firm repaid the fee. A generated procedure is checked by a person against the source rows.

assumptions: Focal role is the community service manager. The task ends when a signed procedures version is filed and exceptions are still handled by the manager. Carrying out the procedure with a client is a later task.
Input contract: objective id, owner, review date, result wanted, program id. Producer is the board member. If the form is empty the manager types the same fields from mail and marks the row manual.
Use the document store's own templates and approval flow before custom code. Template upkeep is counted in incremental hours.
unknowns: Who may sign a procedure when the manager is absent.
Whether the board wants one procedure set or one set per program.
research_questions: How often does a signed procedure cite an objective that has since changed?
Which programs have no named procedure owner?

already_counted.description: Manager edits procedure lines the draft left weak
Manager time in the oversight meeting stays in the step

incremental.description: Update the procedure template when a new program type appears
Board members correct objectives the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: procedures version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many objectives still arrive as free-text mail, so the manager retypes them. The high case assumes the form is used but every version still has a full sign-off. Time in the oversight meeting is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Post activities from volunteers for the week
Assemble the activities brief from those notes

loop.output: a brief that cites activity ids only
loop.check: Every line cites an activity id from the notes
loop.stop: One pass, then stop; leave out any line with no activity id
loop.why_not_simpler: A note's wording varies and a fixed sort cannot summarise it

steps.what: Direct activities of volunteers in the meeting
Sign the activities note for staff and volunteers
Send the signed activities note

tasks.design: Volunteers and staff post activity id, program id, owner and what is blocked, by mail into {DOCS}. A bounded brief groups those notes for the {CALENDAR} meeting. The manager directs the activities in the room. A note is signed in {DOCS} and only that note is sent through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Activity notes were scattered in mail and chat, so a brief could not show which activity it relied on.
tasks.enabler_now: An activity id can tie a note to a program, so the brief can list only notes from this week.
tasks.still_hard: What a volunteer should do next, when two programs clash, is still a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides the priority and says it to the people in the room.

ambition.what: Direct volunteers from a weekly activities brief, not only when a problem appears

tasks.altitude: The meeting stays. The manager spends less of it reconstructing what happened, and can refuse a note that does not match the brief.

reach.task: Carry out the activities named in the signed note
reach.learn: Which activities were directed this week and which are still open

evidence.claim: Directing staff and volunteers is mostly a meeting. A written brief can shorten the recap, not the direction itself.
Digest [S7] describes document drafting from approved text where a person still checks. A brief here may use only the notes submitted that week.

assumptions: Focal role is the community service manager. The task ends when the meeting has happened and the signed activities note is sent. Doing the activity is out of scope.
Input contract: activity id, program id, owner, blocked reason, week. Producer is the volunteer or staff member. If a note has no activity id the brief leaves it on a manual list.
The meeting prior fits this task. Only the brief and the note move. Use the document store's own template before custom code. This design does not schedule or watch staff.
unknowns: Whether volunteers will post notes before the meeting or still arrive with a verbal update.
Who covers direction when the manager is away.
research_questions: What share of activities has no owner this month?
How often does the meeting change the brief?

already_counted.description: Manager corrects the brief before the meeting
Direction time in the room stays with the manager

incremental.description: Keep the brief template aligned with new activity types
Volunteers resubmit notes that lack an activity id

approvals.approved_version: activities note signed after this meeting

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most updates stay verbal, so the brief is thin and the meeting is unchanged. The high case assumes notes are posted but every direction and the sign-off stay with the manager. The meeting itself is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate program quality and resource use

steps.what: Collect resources used on programs this period
Draft a quality note from resource rows

loop.input: resource rows and the note template
loop.output: a note that cites row ids and gives no score
loop.check: Every figure equals a resource row and no sentence scores a person
loop.stop: One pass; drop any sentence with no row id
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether quality is appropriate is not a lookup on the rows

steps.what: Hear volunteers on program quality
Evaluate programs and sign the quality note
File the signed evaluation note

tasks.design: Resource rows already entered in {SPREADSHEET} and {HCM} show program id, hours, spend and owner. A bounded note in {DOCS} cites those rows and does not score a person. The manager evaluates programs with the volunteers, signs the note, and only that note is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quality comments lived in meeting notes, separate from the resource rows, so a draft could not show which figure it used.
tasks.enabler_now: Program id, hours and spend can be read as rows the manager already keeps.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a program is good enough is a judgement about people and context, not a threshold.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides if the quality is appropriate and if the resources were well used.

ambition.what: Evaluate resource use every month, not only at the yearly review

tasks.altitude: Less time hunting figures, the same judgement. The manager can refuse a note that scores a person or cites a missing row.

reach.task: Explain a gap in the resource rows before the evaluation
reach.learn: Which programs are already evaluated and which rows are still blank

evidence.claim: Evaluating program quality is a judgement in a meeting. Figures can be assembled first. A score of a person would be a different and heavier design.
Digest [S10] treats evaluating staff on behaviour or traits as high-risk, and Digest [S11] is a 2026 timing note that puts those duties from 2 December 2027. This design does not score people.
Digest [S12] says a Dutch works council is consulted under article 27 before a system that watches or schedules staff. This view uses fields already entered and adds no watching.
Digest [S15] describes a published report that contained fabricated citations, after which the firm repaid the fee. The quality note is checked against the resource rows.

assumptions: Focal role is the community service manager. The task ends at a signed evaluation note. Pay, discipline and hiring are out of scope.
Input contract: program id, volunteer or staff id, hours, spend, period, owner. Producer is the person who already entered the row. Rows with no program id stay off the note.
The meeting prior fits. Use the spreadsheet's own filters before custom code. If the view is later used to watch staff, consult the works council first. No model score is produced.
unknowns: Whether a works council must be consulted before staff hours are shown on this view.
Who may see another person's hours.
research_questions: What share of programs has no resource row for the last month?
How often does the manager reject the draft note?

already_counted.description: Manager edits the quality note before the review
Evaluation judgement stays in the meeting

incremental.description: Keep the resource filters aligned when a new program is added
Volunteers correct hours the note cannot cite

approvals.approved_version: evaluation note signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes resource rows stay incomplete, so the manager still assembles figures by hand. The high case assumes rows are clean but every evaluation and the sign-off stay manual. No score of a person is counted as a saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Gather current policies on eligibility and benefits
Draft policy options tied to source rows

loop.input: policy rows and the options template
loop.output: options that cite a policy id and name no person
loop.check: Every option cites a policy id and does not name a participant
loop.stop: One pass; drop any option with no policy id
loop.why_not_simpler: The choice of who is eligible is not a fixed rule in the file

steps.what: Participate in the eligibility policies meeting
Sign the organizational policies version
File the signed policies without applying them

tasks.design: Current policy texts sit in {DOCS} with policy id, program id and the benefit they name. A bounded draft offers options and each option cites a policy id. The manager participates in the meeting and signs one policies version. Filing that version does not decide eligibility for any person. A case still goes through {HELPDESK} for a person to decide.
tasks.previous_blocker: Eligibility rules were rewritten from memory in long meetings, so a draft could not show which existing policy it changed.
tasks.enabler_now: Policy id and benefit name can be stored as fields, so a draft can cite them and stop when a citation is missing.
tasks.still_hard: Who may receive a benefit, and what the participant must do, is a policy judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager, with the board, decides eligibility, requirements and benefits. A file does not apply that decision to a person.

ambition.what: Reopen eligibility policy when a repeated case shows a gap, not only once a year

tasks.altitude: The meeting stays. The manager can see which policy lines are cited and can refuse an option that would decide a person on its own.

reach.learn: Which benefits version is current and which lines are still draft

evidence.claim: Setting eligibility and benefits is a meeting about policy. Applying that policy to one participant is a separate, personal decision.
Digest [S1] describes policy-library management that versions policy texts and can summarise them for a person to approve.
Digest [S9] on GDPR article 22 requires a person to decide eligibility and benefits. There is no solely automated decision about a person.
Digest [S15] describes a published report that contained fabricated citations, after which the firm repaid the fee. Policy options are checked against the source rows.

assumptions: Focal role is the community service manager. The task ends at a signed policies version. Deciding one participant's eligibility is out of scope and is never done by the draft.
Input contract: policy id, program id, benefit name, requirement text, source title. Producer is the manager from the current policy file. If a source title is missing the option is left blank.
Use the document store's own versions before custom code. The meeting prior fits this task. Native configuration is tested before any new code.
unknowns: Whether the board or the manager is the final signer on benefits.
Which programs share one eligibility policy.
research_questions: How often does a case show a gap the signed policy does not cover?
Which benefit lines have no source title?

already_counted.description: Manager edits policy options before the meeting
Time in the eligibility meeting stays with the manager

incremental.description: Revise the options template when a benefit type is added

approvals.approved_version: policies version signed in this meeting cycle

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes policy texts stay unstructured, so the draft rarely cites a real id and the meeting is unchanged. The high case assumes texts are clean but every eligibility choice and the sign-off stay with the manager. No decision about a person is treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week stays in supervision and board meetings. Procedure text, evaluation notes and eligibility drafts are ready before those meetings, and the manager still signs them.
reach: Board members receive the signed procedures version instead of a rewritten pack.
Volunteers receive the activities note after the meeting, not a second verbal retelling.
skills_to_grow: Write a procedure so each line points at an objective the board already stated.
Evaluate a program from recorded resource use, without a score of a person.
Keep eligibility and benefits as a signed policy, never as an automatic decision about one person.
role.ambitious_version: Every program has a current signed procedure, a named owner and a review date the board can open.
